summary: Port corrected Luby and Topo coloring primitives with exact deterministic and constrained nondeterministic comparisons.
regressions: 198 cases cover empty/boundary/grid-stride sizes, dynamic body zero, shared groups, split hubs, cliques, high-word colors, pending picks and convergence flags
Nondeterministic first-free choices require a bipartite-matching witness over permitted neighbor observations; immutable fields and all other integer outputs are exact
The Luby correction is separately recorded in 0021-luby-reference-correctness; its shared before/after regressions cover 96 schedules and 129 hash inputs
Native scalar flag kernels preserve their one-thread launch; nontrivial indirect-grid axes and unused triples are checked
differences: Rust reference behavior was corrected in change 0021, not changed silently in TileLang. Both ports now preserve current-round Luby priority competition and wrapping hashes.
Mask helpers scan the 64 colors instead of using target-specific bit-count instructions; integer choices remain equivalent.
A local first-free witness is an explicit memory-observation contract, not a proof of whole-schedule convergence or accelerator memory-model qualification.
Bounded-palette primitives do not complete the full coloring schedule or resolve palette-exhaustion behavior; those remain implementation work. No floating tolerances changed.
